          minLength: 1

          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-

            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com

          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'

          description: >-

        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: >-
                The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName' from the
                stored first and last names.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of the owner's first and last
                names, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where
                LAST3 is the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and
                NNNN is a global 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more
                than the number of owners at the time this owner was created.
              type: string
              example: 'FRA-0011'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where customerCode is the owner's customer code and YY is the
                last two digits of the registration date's year.
              type: string
              example: 'FRA-0011-M20'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier for owners that belong to the same
                household (same last name and address). It is assigned when an
                owner is created with 'sharesHousehold' true and is identical for
                every owner in that household.
              type: string
              example: 'HH-3F2A1B9C4D5E'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The owner's derived duplicate-detection key, formatted
                '<normalizedTelephone>|<email>|<householdId>' where the email and
                household id segments are empty when absent. Two owners are
                treated as duplicates only when their whole identity keys match.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||HH-3F2A1B9C4D5E'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of owners that already existed, at the time this owner
                was created, sharing the same first and last name (compared
                case-insensitively). Excludes the owner itself.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's membership level, a number from 1 to 3 determined on
                creation. It starts at 1, gains 1 when an email is present, gains
                1 when the owner has no namesakes (namesakeCount is 0), and is
                capped at 3 (level 4 is reserved for tenure).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                Whether the owner was created on a day that had already reached
                the bulk-signup threshold: true when more than 80 owners had
                already been created for the owner's registration date at the
                time this owner was created, otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-

                QLD). 'UNKNOWN' when the city is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true

              description: >-

              type: string
              example: 'EMAIL'

          required:

## Summary

I implemented the optional, region-validated `postcode` field for owners.

**What changed:**

1. **`model/Owner.java`** — added a `postcode` column with getter/setter.

2. **`resources/openapi.yml`** — added `postcode` (string) to the `OwnerFields` schema. Since `Owner` is `allOf` `OwnerFields`, the field flows into both the request DTO (`OwnerFieldsDto`) and response DTO (`OwnerDto`); MapStruct maps it by name automatically, and the openapi-generator regenerates both DTOs at build time.

3. **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — added `validatePostcode(postcode, city)`, called during `addOwner`:
   - `null` postcode → accepted (optional, backward-compatible).
   - Must be exactly 4 digits, else 400.
   - Region resolved from a fixed city table (Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD). If the city has no known region, any 4-digit postcode is accepted.
   - Otherwise the value must fall within the region's inclusive range (NSW 2000–2099, VIC 3000–3099, QLD 4000–4099), else 400.
   - 400s are raised via the existing `InvalidOwnerFieldsException`, which the advice already maps to `BAD_REQUEST`.

4. **DDL** (`db/hsqldb`, `db/h2`, `db/mysql`, `db/postgres` `schema.sql`) — added a `postcode VARCHAR(4)` column to the `owners` table. The test profile (`hsqldb`, `ddl-auto=none`) relies on `schema.sql`, so this was required.

**One bug caught during testing:** `Map.of(...).get(null)` throws NPE rather than returning null, so an unknown city crashed the valid-postcode path. I fixed it by resolving the region first and returning early when it's null.

The stored/returned value is preserved verbatim (e.g. `"2000"`), matching the spec.
